g.text: Independent emissions (Climate TRACE)
Source: Climate TRACE Emissions Inventory v5.7.0 (CC BY 4.0, https://zenodo.org/records/20830133), sector
packages for fossil fuel operations, power, manufacturing and mineral extraction, gas co2e_100yr, year 2025,
monthly source-level emissions summed per asset.
Ownership: the packages' *_emissions_sources_ownership_*.csv files give each parent's
overall_share_percent per asset (the public API lists owners without shares, so it is not used for
attribution).
Attribution (`pipeline/ownership.py`): parent emissions = sum of asset emissions x known share. A parent
holding one asset through several paths has its shares summed (capped at 100%). Where a share is unknown, the
low value excludes the asset and the high value includes all of it: a range, never a guess. 12,120 parents; 10,371
are not controlled (>50%) by another real entity (pseudo-holders such as "small shareholder(s)" are ignored).
Matching buyers to parents: only through the reviewed table data/aliases.csv (12 buyer names to 8 parents
so far). Each row states how the buyer relates to the parent and whether Climate TRACE's ownership sectors
cover the group's main emissions (core) or not (partial, e.g. Volkswagen vehicle production, Delta flights).
Partial matches carry a visible warning.
Not comparable to self-reported scope 1. Climate TRACE equity-share estimates differ from company reports by
a factor of two or more in both directions. Spot checks (company figures from secondary sources, still to be
confirmed against primary reports): Shell 123-151 Mt (CT 2025) vs about 50 Mt reported scope 1 (2024, Reuters);
Holcim 35-45 Mt vs about 71 Mt (2024, Tracenable/DitchCarbon); ENGIE 32-39 Mt vs about 22 Mt (2024, Tracenable,
ENGIE SASB disclosure). Netra therefore shows the independent figure with its basis and never computes a single
"coverage" ratio from it.
